title: IoT Software Statistics 2026
description: Comprehensive internet of things statistics for 2026. Market size, adoption rates, ROI data, and key trends for IoT software buyers and vendors.

sections.title: IoT Market Size
sections.body: IoT software is a $35B+ market growing 23% year over year, with 2,760+ adopting organizations, a very large vendor field of roughly 56,900 products, and 16M+ professionals. The small average revenue per vendor confirms a fragmented market of device, connectivity, and data platforms rather than a consolidated one. Buyers should prioritize interoperability standards and security track records — IoT sprawl across many tools (seven per organization on average) makes weak links the usual point of failure. In practice, security and interoperability should gate the shortlist — with roughly 56,900 vendors and a seven-tool average stack, buyers who standardize on compatible, well-audited platforms avoid the weak-link failures that define device ecosystems. With 2,760+ adopting organizations across roughly 56,900 vendors, IoT buyers face the field's widest fragmentation — standardized protocols and audited vendor security histories should precede any feature comparison.

sections.title: Adoption & Usage
sections.body: IoT adoption is even at 60% across both enterprises and SMBs — a rare parity in this dataset — with 69% planning to increase investment and the largest average stack reviewed at seven tools. The flat adoption curve reflects IoT landing where physical operations demand it regardless of company size, while the heavy tool count points to sensor, connectivity, and data platforms piling up. Buyers should consolidate device management before expanding the IoT estate. The 69% intent against seven tools means expansion money exists but should flow through consolidated device-management platforms first — standardizing connectivity before adding sensors.

sections.title: ROI & Business Impact
sections.body: IoT software shows a 163% average 12-month ROI — among the lower returns reviewed — with a 25% productivity improvement, a 20% cost reduction, and positive ROI in about five months. The modest percentages reflect IoT's profile: gains are real but spread across hardware, connectivity, and software layers that each add cost. Buyers should evaluate ROI on the whole program, not the software alone, and be disciplined about decommissioning low-value pilots. The 163% figure sits on the lower end because IoT value spreads across hardware, connectivity, and software layers — program-level accounting plus pilot decommissioning is the discipline that protects the return.

sections.title: Key Trends
sections.body: Seven trends shape the internet of things in 2026, led by AI integration in IoT platforms at 89% adoption — among the highest AI rates in this dataset — cloud-native deployments at 58%, and mobile-first IoT solutions at 57%. Edge computing, device security hardening, telemetry-driven maintenance, and interoperability standards complete the seven. The contents below detail the adoption and investment picture for 2026. The 89% AI rate with 58% cloud-native shows edge telemetry driving value — expect AI at the edge and device-security hardening to dominate 2026 IoT spending priorities.

sections.title: Budget Allocation
sections.body: IoT budgets are the most extreme in this group: $342K per year at enterprises, just $12K in mid-market, and $6K for small businesses. The 57x enterprise-to-mid-market spread reflects the industrial scale of enterprise IoT deployments — fleet, plant, and facility estates — versus SMB pilots. Given the seven-tool average stack, enterprise buyers should audit for redundant platforms as the cheapest source of IoT budget savings. The 57x enterprise-to-mid-market spread marks industrial-scale deployments — enterprise buyers auditing redundant platforms will find the seven-tool stack holds the largest, fastest budget savings of any category reviewed.
